name: William Howard Taft
role: US president (1909–1913) and Chief Justice of the United States (1921–1930)
summary: A judicial conservative Republican who backed protective tariffs, property rights, anti-trust enforcement and a limited but active federal government. He opposed the initiative, referendum and recall of judges, defended representative government and the Constitution's limits, and supported arbitration and a league to enforce peace.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: In 1908 he said he favored no government action that private citizens could do as well or better, while rejecting pure laissez-faire.

public-ownership.rationale: In 1922 he cited failures of government ownership and operation of enterprises suited to private conduct; he backed only narrow exceptions such as postal savings.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Recommended a graduated inheritance tax and sponsored the corporate excise tax and income-tax amendment, but opposed redistributive aims and called for a protective-tariff revenue system.

unions-good.rationale: As judge and president he said unions benefit workers and the public and said he would probably join one as a workman, while condemning boycotts and violence.

property-fundamental.rationale: Wrote that after liberty the right of property is the most important individual right in the Constitution and must not be eliminated.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Pushed trust prosecutions, voluntary federal incorporation under a supervising bureau and a corporate excise tax, but said regulation had reached a point to pause and test it.

cut-welfare.rationale: Warned in 1922 that laws helping individuals into dependence weaken citizenship and called reformers' paternalism excessive; no specific cut to a welfare program is recorded.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Asked Congress to control the manufacture, sale and use of opium and derivatives more rigorously and to suppress interstate traffic in menacing drugs.

strong-leader.rationale: Held that the President may act only under specific grants of power, with no undefined residuum, and criticised Roosevelt's broader stewardship theory.

state-harmful.rationale: Listed wide government functions (defense, regulation, conservation, public health, schools, postal services) as proper and rejected the 'laissez-faire' view.

empower-police-military.rationale: Said army, navy and coast defense spending should not be cut for economy, and urged state constabularies to keep order.

decide-locally.rationale: Argued the central government finds local matters hard to administer, yet favored broad national power under the Constitution on commerce and conservation.

more-religion-public.rationale: Called religion the great stay of morality, said churches need encouragement and universities should encourage worship, and regretted that religious and moral training cannot be united in public schools.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Told Black Americans their hope rested on their own industry, thrift and white Southern friendship, and said Northern efforts to force the franchise had failed.

gradual-change.rationale: Defended representative government and the Constitution's slow amendment process as valuable stability against rapid change from direct democracy devices.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Vetoed a literacy-test restriction on unskilled immigrants, though he continued Asian exclusion and opposed enlarging Ellis Island.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Led the League to Enforce Peace and publicly supported Wilson's League of Nations, with reservations that shifted over time.

free-trade.rationale: Said revision on free-trade principles would close factories, but he also negotiated Canadian reciprocity lowering duties on food and raw materials.

experts-over-public.rationale: Created commissions and a tariff board for expert study and defended appointed life-tenure judges over elected ones, but also accepted a broad electorate.

tax-inheritance.rationale: In 1909 he recommended a graduated inheritance tax as correct in principle and easy to collect; the House adopted it but the Senate dropped it.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Campaigned for protection equal to the difference in cost of production here and abroad, including wages, plus a reasonable profit.

democracy-best.rationale: Said democracy is loved for what it accomplishes, not as a fetish, and he preferred a limited representative republic to pure rule by all.

direct-votes.rationale: Called the initiative and referendum a mistake as general devices that clog government, accepting the referendum only for bonds, local options and amendments.

taxation-theft.rationale: Proposed new inheritance and corporate taxes and called government spending on conservation and defense necessary expense.

total-state.rationale: Rejected socialism and state direction of industry, saying it would end property and individual freedom.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Told Congress in 1909 a deficit of about $100 million must not continue and urged a budget system that balances revenue and expense.

class-collaboration.rationale: Said public education should counter class consciousness and that religion is an antidote for class hatred; he distrusted a class-based labor party.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Wrote the unanimous 1927 opinion upholding exclusion of a Chinese-American child from a white school; he applied precedent rather than stating a view of segregation.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Said Asiatic immigrants who cannot be amalgamated are a problem and discussed the burden of assimilating foreign-born millions.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Said the laissez-faire school that confines government to a police force is outdated and that government rightly interferes to relieve the oppressed and equalise opportunity.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Treated 'We, the people' as the source of political power but called the social-contract consent theory historically untrue.

separated-powers.rationale: Wrote at length defending separation of legislative, executive and judicial powers and checks, including the veto and judicial review.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Wrote the Court opinion limiting picketing to one picket per entrance and as president condemned the secondary boycott, yet defended the right to strike.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Described the President as commander in chief and, in Myers, held that he controls the removal of executive officers.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Preferred a single longer presidential term with no re-election, to free the executive from re-election concerns.

recall-officials.rationale: Argued the recall of executive and legislative officers follows from the referendum, forces governing by passion and robs officials of courage.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Insisted the President has no power beyond express or necessarily implied constitutional or statutory grant.

ban-cartels.rationale: His administration prosecuted the trusts without letup (Standard Oil, Tobacco, Powder and others) and he called the anti-trust act a guard of equality of opportunity.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Fought recall of judicial decisions and judges and defended courts' power to hold laws unconstitutional as a bar on majority action.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Held the Filipinos needed American supervision and training until fit for self-government and rejected immediate independence as premature.

patriotic-education.rationale: Wrote that schools should teach the welfare of the United States and obedience to law and government with ease.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Said the Constitution secures liberty, property and due process against government, with courts enforcing limits and only slow amendment able to change them.

office-by-exam.rationale: His commission said entrance to nearly every subordinate government job should depend on proof by examination, and he backed civil service coverage.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Preached respect for law and obedience as the basis of ordered liberty, urging obedience even to laws one dislikes such as prohibition.

defeat-communism.rationale: In a 1929 letter he said he stayed on the Court to keep the Bolsheviks from getting control.

religion-illusion.rationale: Described religion as the cornerstone of unselfishness and an antidote to class hatred that anarchists and Bolsheviks reject.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Described the Philippine policy as uplifting and training the islanders for self-government and favored free trade with the islands over a purely extractive system.

racial-franchise.rationale: Said the Fifteenth Amendment ought to be observed, never repealed, while accepting race-neutral education tests for voters.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Urged encouragement of churches and worship in universities and counted atheistic radicalism as hostile to constitutional government.

term-limits.rationale: Said it would have been wiser for the President to serve a single six or seven year term.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Wrote that the spirit that sweetens life with love of family, country and God is what constitutional government depends on.

arms-reduction.rationale: In 1910 he proposed a commission to study limiting armaments by international agreement, while also insisting that the United States must stay armed.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Held that workers uniting can command better terms than they could singly with rich employers and that the accumulation of strike funds is legitimate.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: As a judge he held that the right of a non-union man to work for whom and at what price he chooses is sacred and invasion of it cannot be condemned too severely.

women-suffrage.rationale: In 1909 he said he would favor votes for women once they desired it, and in 1913 he put the case in terms of whether it improves government; his later position is not clear.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Said that without parties popular government would be impossible and defended the party system's role.

notes: Taft's positions on direct democracy and the courts were stated most fully in 1913 and 1922. On woman suffrage the record found is conditional (1909, 1913) and later views were not located. The Occasional Papers and Addresses volume found in search is by Henry W. Taft and was not used.
